-#      Binds a filled column data collection to the statement under a name.
-#      Makes the collection visible to the statement as a table named name, by
-#      injecting a common table expression into the parsed statement. The
-#      statement can then be bound, prepared, or executed through the existing
-#      surface; each execution scans the collection's contents at that moment.
-#      Supported statement types are SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and MERGE
-#      INTO; any other type is rejected with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID.
-#      name is a borrowed string view and must be non-empty. A name already
-#      present in the statement's CTE map (from the SQL text or a prior call) is
-#      rejected with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. The binding shadows any catalog table
-#      named name, following standard CTE semantics.
-#      By default the collection's columns bind as col1..colN. Pass column_names
-#      to bind them under caller-chosen names instead, so the statement can
-#      reference them directly (FROM buf) without an alias. When supplied,
-#      column_count must equal the collection's column count; a mismatch is
-#      rejected with ERROR_INPUT_INVALID. Pass (NULL, 0) for the col1..colN
-#      The collection is borrowed: the caller keeps ownership and must keep it
-#      alive while the statement, any prepared statement created from it, and any
-#      result executed from it are live, and must not reset or destroy it while
-#      such a result is live, because result scans reference the collection's
-#      buffers. An empty collection is a valid binding. Multiple collections
-#        description: The statement to bind the collection into. Borrowed; mutated in place.
-#        description: The non-empty identifier the statement references. The empty view {NULL, 0} is rejected.
-#        description: The filled collection to make visible. Borrowed; the caller keeps ownership.
-#        description: Optional. An array of column_count names for the collection's columns, in order. Pass NULL to bind them as col1..colN.
-#        description: The number of names in column_names. Pass 0 to bind the columns as col1..colN; otherwise it must equal the collection's column count.

+      Binds a column data collection to the statement under a name.
+      Makes the collection visible to the statement as a table named `name`, by adding a common table expression to
+      the parsed statement. The statement can then be bound, prepared or executed as usual; each execution reads the
+      collection's contents at that moment, so a prepared statement can be executed again after the collection was
+      cleared and refilled. Supported statement types are SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and MERGE INTO; any other
+      A name the statement already defines as a common table expression, in its SQL text or by a prior call, is
+      rejected with `ERROR_INPUT_INVALID`. The binding shadows any catalog table named `name`, as a common table
+      By default the collection's columns are named col1..colN. Pass `column_names` to name them instead; when
+      supplied, `column_count` must equal the collection's column count. Pass NULL and 0 for the default names.
+      The collection is borrowed: the caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive, and must not clear, reset or
+      destroy it, for as long as the statement, any statement copied or prepared from it, or any result executing it
+      is live. An empty collection is a valid binding. Several collections can be bound under distinct names.
+        description: The statement to bind the collection to. Modified in place.
+        description: The non-empty name the statement refers to the collection by. Borrowed and copied.
+        description: The collection to bind. Borrowed; the caller keeps ownership and must keep it alive.
+        description: Optional. An array of `column_count` names for the collection's columns, in order. Pass NULL for col1..colN.
+        description: The number of names in `column_names`. 0 for the default names; otherwise the collection's column count.
+        description: Optional. On failure, receives an opaque info handle the caller must destroy via `[[error_info_destroy]]`.
